classification.difficultyReason: The hardest part requires finding a total angle without knowing either component: recognise two isosceles triangles, represent their unknown vertex-angle split, and combine their base-angle expressions using the supplied right angle.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals in these diagrams.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with interior D, AD=DB=DC, dashed DB, right angle ADC, and leaders identifying α=BAD and 32°=DBC.

answer.short:
$\alpha=13^\circ$.

Use the two isosceles triangles and angles around $D$.
answer.worked:
$DB=DC$, so $\angle BCD=32^\circ$ (base angles).

$\angle BDC=180^\circ-32^\circ-32^\circ=116^\circ$.

$\angle ADB=360^\circ-90^\circ-116^\circ=154^\circ$.

$AD=DB$, so $\angle DAB=\angle ABD$.

$\alpha=(180^\circ-154^\circ)\div2=13^\circ$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral PQRS with QS diagonal, PS=QS=RS, right angle PSR and full PQR angle arc crossing QS.
spec.mathematics: α is the whole angle PQR, not only SQR.

answer.worked:
$PS=QS=RS$, so both $\triangle PQS$ and $\triangle QRS$ are isosceles.

Let $\angle PSQ=x$ and $\angle QSR=y$. Then $x+y=90^\circ$.

$\angle PQS=(180^\circ-x)\div2$ and $\angle SQR=(180^\circ-y)\div2$.

$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-\frac{x+y}{2}\\\alpha&=180^\circ-45^\circ\\\alpha&=135^\circ\end{align*}$

spec.description: Isosceles triangle PQR with C on PQ, D on QR and segment CD.

answer.worked:
$\angle QCD=180^\circ-162^\circ=18^\circ$ (straight angle).

$\angle CDQ=180^\circ-74^\circ=106^\circ$ (straight angle).

$\angle C Q D=180^\circ-18^\circ-106^\circ=56^\circ$.

$QP=QR$, so $\beta=(180^\circ-56^\circ)\div2=62^\circ$ (equal base angles).

spec.description: Pentagon ABCDE, dashed red BD, BM and DN, vertical perpendicular construction from C, all equal-side ticks and both right-angle marks retained.
spec.mathematics: BC=CD; AB=DE=BM=DN; BCD=108°; DNM=108°; α=BDN; BD parallel AE follows from perpendicular marks.

answer.worked:
$BD\parallel AE$ because both are perpendicular to the vertical construction line.

$\alpha=180^\circ-108^\circ=72^\circ$ (co-interior angles on transversal $DN$).

spec.description: Quadrilateral PQRS with four labelled interior angles.
Quadrilateral DABC with E on DC and segment EB.

answer.worked:
In $\triangle EBC$:

$\begin{align*}2\alpha+24^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=78^\circ\end{align*}$

$\angle ABC=24^\circ+78^\circ=102^\circ$.

$\beta=360^\circ-37^\circ-102^\circ-78^\circ=143^\circ$ (angle sum of quadrilateral $DABC$).
